newsitem.title: ITALY: Confidence vote likely on Italy budget - politician.
newsitem.headline: Confidence vote likely on Italy budget - politician.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government could call a confidence vote in the Senate (upper house) to sweep aside nearly 3,500 amendments to its 1997 budget bill, a senior politician from the governing coalition said on Wednesday.

Gavino Angius, chairman of the Senate's finance commission, said it was "pretty obvious" that the government could resort to a confidence vote to ensure the house meets a December 19 deadline for approving the package.

"So many amendments have been presented that it is practically impossible to think that the budget's passage will be completed on schedule," Angius, a member of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), told reporters.
"Some of the amendments are clearly obstructionist. It is quite legitimate for the government to resort to the instruments that the rules of parliament allow," he said.
Most of the amendments have been submitted by the main opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance and the separatist Northern League.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition has a comfortable majority in the Senate and would not be at risk from a confidence vote.
The budget aims to take 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's deficit through a mix of tax increases, spending cuts and treasury operations.
